## MEDIUM IMPACT

### Component: `hui-map-overview` (Map Card Detail Panel)

**What changed:** In `src/panels/lovelace/cards/map/hui-map-overview.ts`, the element wrapping the person/entity name in the map detail panel was changed from a `<button class="detail-name">` to a `<span class="detail-name" tabindex="-1">`. The click handler (`@click=${this._handleMoreInfo}`) was removed entirely from this element.

**What it affects:** If ha-lcars has any card-mod CSS targeting `button.detail-name` or `hui-map-overview .detail-name` inside the map card's shadow DOM, those selectors would now fail to match because the element is now a `<span>`, not a `<button>`. Reviewing the current preamble shows no explicit `hui-map-overview` or `.detail-name` selectors, so there is no direct breakage in the existing theme source.

However, `<button>` elements carry browser-default styling (cursor, padding, background, border) that `<span>` elements do not. Any indirect styling that relied on `button` reset rules (e.g., `button { background: none; border: none; }` applied globally) will no longer apply to this element. The visual result will depend on whether global button resets in the theme or HA's own base CSS were covering this element. The element may now appear with slightly different baseline styling (no pointer cursor, no button role styling).

**Affected ha-lcars rule:** No direct selector in `preamble.yaml` targets this element. No fix is strictly required, but if the map card's detail name label appears visually different (no pointer cursor, different padding), add an explicit rule:

```yaml
# In card-mod-card-yaml or a targeted card-mod injection for hui-map-card:
"hui-map-card hui-map-overview$": |
  .detail-name {
    cursor: default;
    font-family: var(--font-family);
    background: none;
    border: none;
    padding: 0;
  }
```

### Component: `hui-view-header` (Badge Scroll Row)

**What changed:** In `src/panels/lovelace/views/hui-view-header.ts`, `flex-shrink: 0` was added to `.container:not(.edit-mode) .layout.badges-scroll hui-view-badges`. This prevents the badges row from shrinking when the view header is constrained horizontally.

**What it affects:** If the ha-lcars theme applies any width, flex, or overflow rules to `hui-view-badges` inside a scrolling badges layout (via `card-mod-root-yaml` or other injections), the new `flex-shrink: 0` may interact with those rules. Reviewing the current preamble, there are no explicit selectors for `hui-view-badges` or `.badges-scroll` in the theme. The change is additive and theme-neutral in the current codebase.

The visual effect is that the first badge will no longer be cut off in centered scrolling view headers — this is a bugfix that the theme benefits from passively.

**Affected ha-lcars rule:** None currently. No fix needed unless future badge styling is added.

## LOW IMPACT

### Component: `hui-map-card` — New `show_zone_radius` Config Option

**What changed:** `src/panels/lovelace/cards/types.ts` and `src/panels/lovelace/editor/config-elements/hui-map-card-editor.ts` gained a new optional boolean config key `show_zone_radius`. This controls display of zone radius circles on the map card.

**What it affects:** No CSS impact. The ha-lcars theme does not style zone radius elements. If zone radius circles are rendered as SVG or canvas overlays inside `ha-map`, the theme could optionally style them via a future card-mod injection, but no current rule is affected.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed. Optionally, if users enable `show_zone_radius: true` and the radius circles appear in an LCARS-incompatible color, a future injection into `ha-map$` targeting the zone radius SVG element could remap it to `var(--lcars-ui-secondary)` or similar.

**What changed:** The release notes indicate `ha-chip-base` border radius was fixed (`Fix HaChipBase border radius`, PR #54603). The source file `src/components/chips/ha-chip-base.ts` is listed as changed but its diff is not included in the relevant styling files.

**What it affects:** ha-lcars does not appear to directly target `ha-chip-base` with card-mod selectors in the current preamble. However, chips appear throughout the UI (filter chips, entity chips in automations, etc.) and the border-radius fix may alter their visual appearance. The theme sets `ha-card-border-radius: var(--lcars-outer-radius)` globally and `mdc-shape-small: 0px`, which may or may not cascade into chip border radius depending on which variable `ha-chip-base` consumes.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed immediately. If chips appear with an unexpected radius after this update, audit whether `ha-chip-base` consumes `--ha-chip-border-radius`, `--mdc-shape-small`, or a different token, and override accordingly in `card-mod-root-yaml`.

### Component: `ha-checkbox` — Touch Area Increase

**What changed:** `src/components/ha-checkbox.ts` had its touch area increased (`Increase touch area of ha-checkbox`, PR #54617). The diff is not included in the relevant styling files.

**What it affects:** The ha-lcars theme targets `ha-checkbox` inside the to-do list card via `card-mod-card-yaml`:

```yaml
ha-checkbox {
  border-right: var(--check-border-right) solid var(--lcars-background-color);
  border-left: var(--check-border-left) solid var(--lcars-background-color);
  height: 100%;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  ...
}
```

A larger touch area (typically implemented via padding or a pseudo-element overlay) is unlikely to break the border or height rules, but may affect the visual bounding box of the checkbox within the to-do list row if it adds padding that shifts internal layout.

**Suggested fix:** No fix needed immediately. Monitor to-do list card checkbox alignment after this update. If the checkbox appears misaligned within `ha-check-list-item` rows, re-examine the `height: 100%` and `display: flex` rules on `ha-checkbox` in `card-mod-card-yaml`'s to-do section.
